purpose: Four directed loading illustrations; runtime selects the final edge of City—MountainRoad—AlpineVillage.
common: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: final full-screen loading illustration for Bar Promenade, a melancholic, oppressive, mundane PS1-inspired game. Create a finished artistic painting with restrained visible oil/gouache brushwork, dry-brushed edges and fine static worn-print grain. A coherent painterly work, hand-painted shapes, not a screenshot, not a photoreal image, not a glossy 3D render. Preserve the ordinary worn functional design language of the supplied game reference. Cold charcoal and desaturated grey-green with restrained dirty ochre and a few weak practical lights; substantial readable midtones. Melancholic and depressive through distance, solitude and patient heavy architecture. No catastrophe, gore, monsters, fantasy, mystical symbols, heroic spectacle, tourist scenery, text, numbers, logos, watermark, frame, UI, or painted progress bar. The world is unnamed, no specific real car brand. Landscape 16:9 composition, intended 2048x1152 or larger. Important subjects in the central 60% width and central 65% height so 4:3 and ultrawide crops retain them. Bottom 15% is a quiet dark low-detail painted ground or atmosphere for a separate progress bar; do not introduce a literal black strip.

Direction: ALPINE VILLAGE TO MOUNTAIN ROAD. A small old rectangular enclosed cableway gondola in weathered dark green, broad rectangular green-grey windows, shallow roof, single steel hanger physically joined to its cable, the SAME design as the ascending companion painting. View from beside the upper station looking down along the descending cable as the small gondola leaves into heavy grey-green atmospheric depth, around centre and 18% picture width. At upper-left middle ground a fragment of the ordinary snow-covered corrugated station canopy and supporting dark steel columns, with one restrained warm light under shelter, stands against a close confining rock wall. A tiny partly obscured patch of old wooden village wall and warm window may appear behind the canopy at the picture edge, no whole village vista. Strong oblique snowfall, dirty snow piled on the platform lip, worn metal, no open Alpine panorama. Perspective and visible connection to the upper station clearly establish DESCENT, distinct from ascent. Warmth is left behind; the destination below is only a dim functional support disappearing in cold haze. Bottom foreground is quiet, dark and spare. Match the companion oil/gouache artwork, static print grain, restrained palette and readable muted values. No faces, signs or text.

Input image 1 is the companion cableway PAINTING: preserve its exact gondola design, brushwork, fine grain and muted colours. Change to the entirely new DESCENDING composition described. Image 2 is the GAME upper village reference for restrained warm windows and snowfall; image 3 is the GAME utilitarian station structure reference. Cables must be physically correct, two distinct parallel runs visibly spanning from the upper station behind the viewer, through the gondola's hanger grip, and continuing downhill past the gondola toward the distant support. Never terminate a line at the gondola and never cross cables.

scenes.city-to-mountain: Direction: CITY TO MOUNTAIN ROAD. A solitary battered boxy high-roof period SALOON car, faded muddy ochre-brown paint, squared boot and rear window, practical thin bumpers, mismatch passenger door, same silhouette and proportions as the car in the supplied game reference. View from some distance behind and slightly to its left, the entire small car around 18% of picture width, driving away along damp asphalt inside a long utilitarian concrete tunnel. Two tiny dim red rear lights; no other traffic. A heavy arch and transverse concrete joints repeat into shadow. A narrow cold grey-green opening far ahead suggests the rocky road beyond, with a little dirty snow at its margins, never a mountain panorama. A few weak old utilitarian lamps high on the tunnel wall, soft broken reflections on damp road, solid old concrete rather than crumbling ruin. Camera low but not dramatic, strongly receding quiet space; the car is isolated around the centre, with dark foreground beneath it. One still painting of leaving the city. Reference image is design/color grounding ONLY, not an edit target: create this entirely new tunnel composition.
scenes.mountain-to-city: Direction: MOUNTAIN ROAD TO CITY. The SAME battered boxy high-roof period SALOON car, faded muddy ochre-brown paint, squared body, mismatch passenger door and modest warm headlamps. Create a genuinely different composition: camera just outside the CITY end of the tunnel, looking obliquely back into the dark arch as the small car approaches and emerges toward the viewer, front three-quarter view. The heavy tunnel mouth occupies the central-right middle ground; a tired retaining wall and a few ordinary indistinct grey city-edge facades and utility poles disappear into low grey-green haze at the left edge. No skyline spectacle or landmarks, no trees or scenery dominating. The same worn wet concrete, small utilitarian tunnel wall lamps, damp asphalt holding thin weak amber headlight streaks; no other traffic, no visible detailed faces. Around 20% picture-width car within the centre, lower foreground open and dark. Sense of returning somewhere that has not waited for you. Match the companion painting's brushwork, grain, values and restrained palette, but do not mirror its composition.
scenes.mountain-to-village: Direction: MOUNTAIN ROAD TO ALPINE VILLAGE. A small old utilitarian enclosed rectangular cableway gondola ascending toward an upper rock cut. Weathered dark desaturated green lower metal panels, broad rectangular green-grey windows, shallow practical roof, single steel hanger correctly connected to a taut cable, modest two-to-four-person proportions like the game's cabins, no modern bubble gondola. Seen from behind and slightly below, isolated around centre, roughly 18% picture width. Cable recedes UPWARD into a narrow man-made notch through a huge close dark snow-streaked rock wall, in thick oblique snowfall. The ground below is only muted grey-green depth; the rock is a confining mass, not a scenic outline or dramatic peak. One distant utilitarian support is enough. Village houses and lights must NOT be visible from the lower side of the ridge. Paint fine streaks of blown snow but keep the gondola and rock cut readable; empty lower space in deep cold haze. An ordinary journey into silence, with no threat or supernatural element. Match the companion painting's restrained oil/gouache handling and old-print grain. Game station and village references ground materials/weather, not literal composition.
